title: SPF explained
caption: SPF numbers measure one thing only: how much longer UVB rays take to redden your skin compared to no protection. They say nothing about UVA — the rays that drive pigmentation and collagen breakdown, which matter more in year-round Gulf sun. A broad-spectrum label means both UVA and UVB are covered; without it, a high SPF number gives false confidence. In 40°C heat with AC sweat cycles, reapplication every two hours is what keeps the number on the bottle relevant. Knowing what SPF actually measures — and what it doesn't — changes how you read a label. Not medical advice, just the honest basics. Learn more at cliniclick.ae
